integer_transfer_obstruction.claim_status: abc for integers is OPEN; no analogue is proved here
integer_transfer_obstruction.obstruction_1_no_derivation: Every ring derivation D: Z -> Z is identically zero. D(1)=D(1*1)=2D(1) forces D(1)=0, and additivity forces D(n)=0 for all n. So the Wronskian W = a'b - ab' is identically 0 over Z -- the invariant that carries the whole polynomial proof simply does not exist.
integer_transfer_obstruction.obstruction_2_no_size_drop: deg plays the role of the archimedean valuation at infinity, and the polynomial proof crucially uses deg(P') = deg(P) - 1: differentiation drops size by exactly one while respecting Leibniz. There is no operation on Z that reduces log|n| by a bounded amount while obeying a product rule. log|n| is the integer analogue of deg, but nothing plays the role of d/dx.
integer_transfer_obstruction.obstruction_3_p_derivations_are_local: Buium p-derivations delta_p (delta_p(x) = (x^p - (something))/p) give an arithmetic differential calculus, but they are p-adic and see one prime at a time; there is no single global object playing the role of the Wronskian whose archimedean size is controlled. The arithmetic derivative n' (p'=1, Leibniz) exists but has no deg-drop property and can grow, so it yields no Mason-Stothers analogue either.
integer_transfer_obstruction.consequence: Mason-Stothers is a one-page theorem; integer abc is a famous open problem precisely because the derivation/size-drop mechanism has no faithful archimedean integer counterpart.
